title: Why You Forget Why You Walked In

scenes.narration: You walk into a room, and instantly forget why you came in.
scenes.art: a confused young adult frozen in a kitchen doorway with a big question mark above their head, comedic

scenes.narration: You stand there. You look around. You open the fridge for no reason.
scenes.art: a young adult standing in front of an open glowing fridge at night staring blankly, comedic

scenes.narration: It's not just you. And it might actually be the door's fault.
scenes.art: a cartoon door with a sneaky mischievous face grinning, glowing purple doorway

scenes.narration: In one experiment, people carried objects through a virtual building. Sometimes across a big room, sometimes through a doorway.
scenes.art: a simple video game style virtual building with rooms and doors, a small character carrying a box through a doorway

scenes.narration: After walking through a door, they forgot more than after walking the same distance inside one room.
scenes.art: a split scene: on the left a person walking across one room remembering a box, on the right a person walking through a door with the memory floating away like a balloon

scenes.narration: So they tried it with real rooms too. Same result.
scenes.art: a real looking cozy apartment hallway with several doors, a student holding a box looking puzzled

scenes.narration: The theory: your brain chops life into scenes, like a movie. A doorway is a scene cut.
scenes.art: a long film strip where each frame is a different room connected by doorways, a cartoon brain holding scissors

scenes.narration: When the scene changes, details from the last scene get filed away. Including why you walked in.
scenes.art: a cartoon brain filing a sticky note labeled with a scissors icon into a tall cabinet drawer and closing it

scenes.narration: Your brain isn't broken. Clearing out the old scene probably helps you focus on the new one. Mostly.
scenes.art: a cartoon brain sweeping old memory clouds out of a room with a broom, smiling, slightly sweaty

scenes.narration: And in the study, going back to the first room didn't really help. Which is awkward, because that's exactly what we all do.
scenes.art: a young adult walking backwards through a doorway into the living room looking around hopefully, comedic

scenes.narration: So next time, try saying it out loud before you go. I'm getting the scissors.
scenes.art: a young adult pointing forward confidently while walking through a door, a speech bubble with a scissors icon

scenes.narration: Now, what were we talking about?

post.title: Why you forget why you walked into a room 🚪🤔
post.description:
It might be the door's fault. Scientists found that walking through a doorway makes you forget more than walking the same distance in one room.

Source: Radvansky, Krawietz & Tamplin (2011) Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology
